owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to the contract's branch.
Never defer: no "later", "follow-up", "out of scope". If blocked: what blocks, what you tried, what you need; then continue with the next task.
Root cause, then fix: file:line + mechanism. No weakening tests, raising timeouts, skips, relaxed assertions.
No silent scope cuts: never lower targets, caps or test sizes without owner approval.
Never bypass guards: no --no-verify, no bypass env vars, no skip flags.
Deliver continuously: one task per commit, pushed to the contract's branch as it goes green.
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.

tasks.title: Decision record
requirements: Relationships between people, teams, departments, projects, programmes, decisions, artefacts and evidence

Establish an organisation-level knowledge and work graph connecting people, teams, departments, projects, programmes, customers or other business entities, commitments, decisions, artefacts, risks, issues, dependencies and evidence.

Keep each project independently governed. Shared organisational awareness must not erase project scope, ownership, approval authority, confidentiality or the distinction between a local project fact and an organisation-wide policy.

The system may propose assumptions, identify gaps and raise potential issues, but it must show the source, context, freshness and confidence of each finding. A model-generated inference is a hypothesis to validate, not a new organisational fact or an authorised change.

Do not require staff to manually copy every update into a central knowledge base. Capture and reconcile useful work state through the existing project store, event history, integrations and approved agent workflows, with explicit controls over what is shared.
The existing vault.mjs, graph and retrieval modules are useful foundations. They do not by themselves establish this wider organisational intelligence capability.
